description: CoastSeg is a Python toolkit with browser and notebook workflows for deriving shoreline locations from satellite imagery. The JOSS article describes image selection, waterline detection, tide correction, transects and saved sessions; the own repository provides install and use documentation. Spatial coverage is the coastal region selected, and temporal coverage is the available imagery. The repository reports GPL-3.0. Shoreline histories can help calibrate coastal-erosion or flood-defence exposure simulations. A caveat is that cloud cover, waterline extraction, tidal correction and wave runup all affect an estimated shoreline. A shoreline change series does not itself predict defence failure or storm-surge height. Image-provider terms and availability remain separate from the software licence. No directly related catalogue record was established. The article and own README were inspected without downloading satellite imagery or running a workflow.
name: CoastSeg satellite-derived shoreline workflows
